match.reason: The closest bank point, e-unemployment, covers frictional and seasonal unemployment and the effects of unemployment as well as cyclical and structural, so it is broader than this point, which teaches only cyclical and structural unemployment and how long each lasts.

draft.title: Types of unemployment
card: unemployment caused by weak aggregate demand in a downturn. Firms sell less, so they cut output and jobs. It falls as the economy recovers.
unemployment caused by a mismatch between the skills or location of workers and the jobs on offer. It happens when an industry shrinks or changes, or when jobs are in a different place.

Structural unemployment tends to last longer, because workers need time to retrain or move. More spending in the economy does not fix it quickly, because the new jobs need different skills or are somewhere else.
To tell them apart, ask why the jobs are missing. If jobs are missing across many industries, think cyclical. If jobs exist but workers do not fit them, think structural.
draft.remember: Cyclical: too few jobs overall in a downturn. Structural: jobs exist, but workers do not match them.

a.q: A recession cuts household spending, and shops, cafés and factories across Victoria all lay off workers. What type of unemployment is this?
opts: Cyclical, because demand for goods has fallen
Structural, because workers lack the skills needed
Cyclical, because workers have moved to other regions
Structural, because demand for goods has fallen
a.why: Weak spending hit many industries at once, so firms cut jobs. That is cyclical unemployment. It is not structural, because the workers' skills and locations did not stop matching the jobs. The jobs were lost because demand fell.
a.clue: Why did firms in many industries cut jobs at the same time?

b.q: A car plant in Geelong closes for good. Local jobs in aged care are available, but many former plant workers do not have the qualifications. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is structural, and likely to last longer than cyclical
It is structural, and likely to end once demand recovers
It is cyclical, and likely to last longer than structural
It is cyclical, and likely to end once demand recovers
b.why: Jobs exist in aged care, but the workers' skills do not match them. That is structural unemployment. Because the workers need time to retrain, it tends to last longer. Higher spending alone would not quickly fix it, which is why the cyclical options are wrong.
b.clue: Are jobs missing overall, or do the workers not fit the jobs on offer?

a.best: Cyclical, because demand for goods has fallen

b.best: It is structural, and likely to last longer than cyclical
